Evidence: Per-mouse rank separation marginal; not cell-state specific (CP > Areg); not tissue-specific (SM also increases); does not survive DESeq2 (padj=0.27).
Interpretation: CXCL12 is a general mesenchymal exercise response. Not a headline claim. The Fndc5/Areg finding (NB11) remains the stronger, more specific signal.

Evidence: All stromal states (CP, Areg, WAT_IPC, pre_CP) increase CXCL12 with exercise. Pattern across SC/SH/TC/TH characterizes whether obesity suppresses it.
Interpretation: If obesity suppresses CXCL12 (mirrors CCL2 elevation), the inverse relationship across four conditions strengthens the switch hypothesis.

Evidence: CCL2 suppression is NOT general across all stromal states — it is concentrated in fibroblasts (-2.36 summed delta) and WAT_IPC (-1.44). Areg and CP show smaller changes.
Interpretation: The asymmetry is the interesting part: all stromal cells increase CXCL12 broadly, but only specific cell states (fibroblast, WAT_IPC) shut down CCL2. This differential suppression suggests cell-state-specific regulatory mechanisms.

Evidence: CCL2↓ from fibroblasts/WAT_IPC should reduce M1 infiltration. CXCL12↑ from all stromal cells should promote CXCR4+ immune cell retention. M1/M2 proportion data tests whether the proportion shift matches the signal shift.
Interpretation: If CCL2 tracks M1 abundance across the four conditions, this links the stromal chemokine switch to the macrophage polarization story from the original paper.

Finding: Relationship to Yang et al. RANK-RANKL-OPG
Evidence: Yang et al. showed exercise decreases OPG in IPCs/fibroblasts, allowing RANKL to activate M2 macrophages. Our CCL2/CXCL12 switch is a parallel mechanism.
Interpretation: Two complementary stromal→macrophage axes: RANK-RANKL for M2 activation, CCL2/CXCL12 for M1 suppression and homeostatic positioning. Not in the paper.
